market_name: OpenAI announces it has achieved AGI before 2027?

predictions.asset: AI semiconductor/mega-cap tech equity via Nvidia

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the market probability move coincides with any OpenAI/Microsoft press wire, and whether NVDA is moving on its own (options flow, sector-wide vs idiosyncratic).
time_plan.1h: Compare NVDA move to SOX/semis index — if the whole sector moves it is macro, not AGI-specific; discount the mapping.
time_plan.2h: Look for credible reporting corroborating any AGI-related announcement; absent that, treat the market move as noise.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether any headline materialized; if none, expect mean-reversion of both the prediction market and any tech-equity blip.
time_plan.12h: Close out research view: confirm whether NVDA net move exceeded normal daily vol and whether it was attributable to AI-milestone news at all.

predictions.reasoning: OpenAI is private, so the only listed proxies for an 'AGI achieved' signal are its ecosystem beneficiaries — Nvidia (compute demand) and Microsoft (largest backer). In theory a sharp jump in the implied probability of a near-term AGI announcement could presage a genuine capability/product breakthrough that lifts AI-compute demand narratives. In practice this is an extremely low base-rate, definitionally fuzzy, long-dated (through Dec-2026) question; a move in its odds is far more likely to reflect speculative retail flow or a semantic redefinition of 'AGI' than leaked material information. The link from a private lab's self-declared milestone to a 12h move in a specific chip stock is very weak and easily swamped by macro, rate, and earnings noise.

predictions.asset: OpenAI's largest public backer via Microsoft

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Verify no MSFT-specific news; check if prediction-market move is a single large order vs broad repricing.
time_plan.1h: Benchmark MSFT vs QQQ to strip out index beta.
time_plan.2h: Scan for OpenAI governance or partnership headlines that could flip the sign.
time_plan.6h: Check whether any move persists or reverses; long-dated speculative markets rarely lead real MSFT moves.
time_plan.12h: Document whether the mapping produced any measurable, attributable MSFT move; expect not.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft holds the most direct public-equity exposure to OpenAI's economics and IP. A credible near-term AGI announcement could be read as bullish (product/monetization edge) or bearish (governance turmoil, capex intensity, or profit-sharing complications), so even conditional on a real signal the sign is ambiguous. Given AGI has no agreed operational definition and the resolution window runs through end-2026, a change in this market's odds carries very little clean information for MSFT over a 12h horizon.

evidence_used: Market question resolves Yes only if OpenAI officially announces AGI before Dec 31 2026 — a long-dated, low base-rate event
OpenAI is a private company; nearest liquid public proxies are Nvidia (compute) and Microsoft (largest backer)
'AGI' lacks a precise operational definition, making resolution and interpretation ambiguous
Mega-cap tech and semis are heavily driven by macro/rates/earnings, which dominate any single-event signal over 12h
uncertainty_notes: Direction is genuinely ambiguous even conditional on a real signal (bullish product edge vs bearish governance/capex read)
A move in the market probability likely reflects speculative flow or definitional debate, not leaked material info
12h horizon is too short for a private-lab milestone narrative to reliably transmit to a specific stock
Threshold of 700bps is very unlikely to be met absent an actual confirmed announcement

llm_justification.summary: This market maps only weakly to public assets: OpenAI is private, so the sole listed proxies are ecosystem beneficiaries Nvidia and Microsoft. AGI is ill-defined, the horizon runs through end-2026, and the base rate is tiny, so a shift in implied odds most plausibly reflects speculative or semantic noise rather than leaked information. Even if a genuine signal existed, the equity sign is ambiguous. Both mappings are low-confidence, unclear-direction, and below the 700bps tradable threshold — this is explicitly a weak, non-actionable signal.
key_assumptions: No listed instrument directly tracks OpenAI; NVDA/MSFT are the closest liquid proxies
A prediction-market odds move need not correspond to any public news or real capability change
Macro and sector factors dominate single-stock moves over a 12h window
failure_modes: The move is pure speculation/redefinition of 'AGI' with zero fundamental content
The signal is already public (an announcement everyone has seen) so no edge remains
NVDA/MSFT exposure to an OpenAI self-declared milestone is weak and easily reversed
Sign ambiguity: a real announcement could be read as bearish (governance/capex/profit-sharing) rather than bullish
Any equity blip mean-reverts within the 12h window and is indistinguishable from noise
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
